desc:
Real-time dashboard updates with live data let key numbers change on screen the moment something happens. Ecom Swift LLC adds live panels and feeds to your own app using WebSockets or server-sent events, built to stay calm, reconnect and spare your server.

## What are real-time dashboard updates?

Real-time updates push new information from your server to the browser without the user reloading the page. A new order appears in a feed, an active-users counter ticks up, or a progress bar follows a running job. The server sends a small message whenever something changes, and the page updates just that part.

Two common technologies do this. WebSockets keep a two-way connection open. Server-sent events keep a one-way stream from server to browser, which is simpler when the page only needs to listen.

## Why live data matters, and when it does not

Some information loses value as it ages. A support team watching a queue, a seller tracking new orders or an operator monitoring a running import all need to see changes straight away. Waiting for a refresh means missed events and repeated manual reloads.

But not every number needs to be live. A monthly revenue chart gains nothing from constant updates, and live connections cost server resources. The right approach is to make a few important panels live and leave the rest as normal pages. We help you choose which, so you gain the speed where it counts without raising complexity everywhere.

## What a good live dashboard includes

- Live panels only where speed adds value.
- Smooth value changes, without flicker or jumping layouts.
- Automatic reconnection after a lost connection or a sleeping laptop.
- A fallback to normal refresh when live updates are not available.
- A visible connection status, so users know the numbers are current.
- A live activity feed that adds new items at the top.
- Updates limited to the data each user is allowed to see.
- Separate message channels for each customer account.
- Highlights or sounds for new items, which users can turn off.
- A hosting setup able to carry many open connections.

## How we build it

We begin by choosing the screens and numbers that need to be live, and how quickly each must update. For many panels, server-sent events are enough and keep things simple. Where users also send data back instantly, we use WebSockets.

We add the live channel to your server, publish events when records change, and connect the panels in your front-end. Access rules are applied to every message, so a user only receives what they could already see. The Basic package delivers one live panel with reconnection and a fallback. Standard adds several panels, a live feed, a status indicator and a load check with a set number of simulated users. Premium adds more panels, highlights, per-account channels, a hosting setup that scales and a larger load check. We test by dropping the connection on purpose to confirm that it recovers.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Make live only the numbers where seconds matter.
- Send small messages, not whole pages of data.
- Check permissions on every message sent.
- Show users when the connection is lost.
- Test with many users connected at once.

**Avoid:**
- Making every screen live by default.
- Letting numbers flicker or rearrange while people read.
- Sending other customers' data down a shared channel.
- Leaving users with stale numbers and no warning.
- Running connections on hosting that cannot hold them open.

## Who this is for

This service suits operations teams that watch queues, sales dashboards and job progress. It suits SaaS founders adding a live activity feed, and marketplaces where new orders or messages must appear immediately. It also fits apps that are already live, since panels can be added one at a time.

## What we need from you

Tell us which numbers or lists should update live, how fresh they must be, and how many users might watch at once. Send a staging link or a description of how your server is hosted.

We need developer or collaborator access to your code repository and hosting where the platform supports it. We never need your passwords. After you order, we reply with a short checklist and keep you updated until the live panels are working.
